title: Scheme nodal families are preserved and reflected by etale postcomposition
statement: Let $C,T,S$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $g:C\to T$ be a morphism and let $e:T\to S$ be etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], without any surjectivity assumption on $e$. Call a morphism of schemes nodal of relative dimension one if it is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and for every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and every geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ of the target [def-weil-geometric-point], its fibre [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-pc-fibre-product] is empty or pure of dimension one [def-weil-pure-dimension], with every point either smooth over $\Omega$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] or an ordinary node. Here an ordinary node is a closed point [def-weil-closed-points] whose maximal-ideal-adic completed local $\Omega$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] is isomorphic to $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Then $g$ is nodal of relative dimension one if and only if $e\circ g:C\to S$ is nodal of relative dimension one. Empty schemes and empty fibres are allowed, and no properness, connectedness, quasi-compactness or Noetherian assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0CD8 (lemma-nodal-family-postcompose-etale), forward implication; reverse implication by base change Tag 0C5B (lemma-base-change-nodal-family) and the open graph of a morphism to an etale scheme; definition-nodal-family, Tag 0C5A.

proof.text: Put $h=e\circ g$. First assume $g$ is nodal. By [def-weil-etale-morphism], $e$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Since $g$ is flat and $e$ is flat, [lem-pc-flat-compose] (with $X=C$, $Y=T$, $Z=S$) makes $h=e\circ g$ flat. Since $g$ and $e$ are locally of finite presentation, [lem-sbc-locally-finite-presentation-composition] (with $U=C$, $X=T$, $a=g$, $f=e$) makes $h$ locally of finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 0CD8, lemma-nodal-family-postcompose-etale, first paragraph; expand composition of affine presentations

proof.text: Fix any algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$. Put $T_s=T\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ and $C_s=C\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. The map $T_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits](1), hence unramified by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Apply [lem-trf-unramified-field-fibre-decomposition] over the field $\Omega$: $T_s$ is a possibly empty disjoint union of open and closed spectra $\operatorname{Spec}L_i$, with $L_i/\Omega$ finite separable. Each $L_i=\Omega$ as an $\Omega$-algebra: the minimal polynomial of every element is irreducible and splits into linear factors over an algebraically closed field, so has degree one. Consequently the pieces give geometric points $t_i:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ above $s$. No finiteness of the set of pieces is used.

source.place: Tag 0CD8, geometric-fibre expansion of the second paragraph; Morphisms Tag 02G7, lemma-unramified-over-field (1)

proof.text: Take inverse images of the open and closed pieces $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\subset T_s$ under $C_s\to T_s$. This partitions $C_s$ into open and closed subschemes $D_i$. By [def-pc-fibre-product], $D_i\cong C\times_{T,t_i}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ over $\Omega$: both schemes represent pairs $(c,a)$ with $g(c)=t_i(a)$, and the inverse maps are the unique maps with these projections. Since $g$ is nodal, each nonempty $D_i$ is pure of dimension one and its points are smooth or ordinary nodes. Every irreducible component of a disjoint open partition lies in one piece: an irreducible subset meeting two pieces would be the union of two disjoint nonempty relatively open subsets. Its maximality as an irreducible closed subset is then exactly maximality within that closed piece. Thus the components and their dimensions in [def-weil-pure-dimension] agree. Local rings, their maximal ideals and completions are identical on an open subscheme; smoothness at a point means smoothness on an open neighbourhood. A point closed in $D_i$ is closed in $C_s$ since $D_i$ is closed. Hence $C_s$ has exactly the required fibre property. This proves that $h$ is nodal.

source.place: Tag 0CD8, second paragraph, after geometric splitting: explicit clopen-piece argument

proof.text: Conversely assume $h$ is nodal. Form $P=C\times_ST$ with projection $p:P\to T$ and graph $j=(1_C,g):C\to P$. Since $p$ is the base change of $h$, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] show that $p$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. By [def-weil-etale-morphism] and [def-weil-unramified-morphism], $\Delta_e:T\to T\times_ST$ is an open immersion. The graph $j$ is its base change along $P\to T\times_ST$, $(c,t)\mapsto(g(c),t)$: the two projections and the relation $g(c)=t$ give inverse maps by [def-pc-fibre-product]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] makes $j$ an open immersion. It is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1), hence flat and locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Since $p\circ j=g$ with $j$ and $p$ both flat and locally of finite presentation, [lem-pc-flat-compose] makes $g$ flat and [lem-sbc-locally-finite-presentation-composition] (with $a=j$, $f=p$) makes $g$ locally of finite presentation.

source.place: Reverse implication: open graph of a morphism to an etale target; Tag 01JY and the defining open diagonal of an unramified morphism

proof.text: For any $t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ over an algebraically closed field, set $s=e\circ t$. Repeat step 2 for this $s$. The lift $t$ gives a section $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T_s$. Its image is one of the point-spectrum pieces: a map from a one-point spectrum selects one piece, and the only $\Omega$-algebra endomorphism of $\Omega$ is the identity. The corresponding piece of $C_s$ is, by the projection argument of step 3, exactly $C_t=C\times_{T,t}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. Since $h$ is nodal, $C_s$ is empty or pure of dimension one with smooth points and ordinary nodes. A clopen piece has the same component dimensions, local rings and completions, by the explicit arguments of step 3. A closed point of $C_s$ in that piece stays closed there. Thus $C_t$ has the required fibre property. Together with step 4 this proves $g$ nodal. All arguments allow empty pieces and empty schemes, and never require $e$ surjective, proper, quasi-compact or separated.

source.place: Reverse implication: apply the same geometric-fibre decomposition to the chosen lift t
